title: 7-round AES-256: Basic MITM tradeoff: selected subkeys

target.description: Reduced-round AES-256, with initial whitening. Section5's partial-decryption boundary uses the final-round byte positions; Section2 describes omission of final MixColumns. Costs follow that source convention. Steps2–5 identify four whitening-key bytes, one round1 byte, all sixteen final-round-key bytes and four transformed penultimate-round-key bytes (200 bits of round-key material); these are not asserted to be independent master-key bits.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; the source attack derivation treats searched round-key bytes without using schedule relations.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key restriction.
setting.plaintext_model: Source 2^32 chosen-plaintext structure; Step2's diagonal coordinates differ from the cost paragraph's first-column description. Repeat with changed plaintext sets according to the tradeoff parameters.
assumptions: Offline table generation and online search have different native work units and are kept separate.
The source p.122 converts 2^88 partial decryptions to 2^80 encryption equivalents using its stated factor of 2^8. This conversion is recorded, not independently calibrated.
Step6's remaining-key enumeration has no separate numerical budget; the online figure describes the matching/search phase.
Section5 uses absolute function-value sequences and guesses a transformed penultimate-round-key byte.
Section5.1 samples a 1/n1 fraction of functions and repeats online search n2 times, with n1,n2>1.

success.description: Conditional source-model envelope for correct identification of the200bits of selected round-key material in the raw/basic seven-round construction, not complete master-key recovery. Adopt the intended corrected25-parameter factorization and plaintext coordinates, the same generic right-sequence marginal model for each of four target outputs, and the conditional uniform2048-bit wrong-sequence/table-hit model for every tested wrong guess given its precomputed table. This conditional hit upper bound is an explicit model premise, not inferred from unconditional uniformity. All four targets may use the same full allotted n2 acquired structures rather than forcing later targets to use only the first successful structure. With table reduction n1 and n2 allotted structures per target, four-marginal union bounding and at most4*n2*2^80 tested target/guess pairs give max(0,1-4*(1-1/n1)^n2-2^-1766*n2/n1). No inter-target or inter-guess independence is required; the within-target sampling assumptions of Equation7 remain. Here M denotes exactly the stated source-inspired probability model; its inequality is mathematical within that model, whereas actual AES success is only a heuristic interpretation. The complete-table point uses n1=n2=1. At n2=4*n1 the four-hit term is at least1-4*exp(-4), about0.926737, before the modeled false-match subtraction. This is a heuristic source-model estimate, not a rigorous AES distribution bound or a fixed-time cap. It applies only when the stored structures and table are feasible and the source matching-phase work estimate is adopted. Literal printed-function/coordinate conflicts, finite-domain/query limits, and native cost uncertainty remain. Residual-master-key completion, WLH new constructions and Kara/XOR-normalized signatures are excluded. The selected200bits are round-key material, not independent master-key bits. Model applicability requires a nonempty finite target table of at most \(2^{200}/n_1\) ordered256-byte functions, a positive integer n2 of usable structures, and the stated retained-fraction marginal for each target; the sampled branch has n1,n2>1. No all-parameter feasibility claim is made.

components.description: Section5.1 Equation7, n1,n2>1: reduce the complete table by n1 and repeat with n2 input sets under the source sampling model. The source rounds its limits to63% at n2=n1 and98% at n2=4n1. The actual finite admissible domain, uniformity and dependence remain unproved; the formula is one table hit, not completed recovery.

review.scope: Verified the conditional source-model composition for the already priced partial-key matching phase: intended complete-table coverage, four target marginals from Equation7 and target symmetry, and a union bound over wrong-guess tests. Verification is of this explicit conditional model, not resolution of printed-formula/coordinate conflicts, a proof of actual AES random-sequence laws, full-parameter feasibility, cost calibration or complete master-key output.

field_conflicts.label: Printed function expansion
field_conflicts.description: The recurrence preceding Proposition2 omits the third-round S-boxes. Printed Equation(1) also differs from the second-round diagonal expressions immediately above it. A separately derived 25-parameter AES factorization passes local component tests; the printed expressions are preserved as discrepant. DTCB09 explicitly corrects Equation1 and the C3_22/C3_44 expansions in Equations2/4, while stating that these errors do not affect DS08 attack applicability. Separate corrected AES factorization is supported, not the literal print.
